terra.problem: The passage does not say Abram has a tent at this moment.
The passage does not place Abram in his front yard when he hears the promise.
Saying Abram could use a good address invents a need the text does not give him.
The passage does not say that speaking Abraham's name is itself saying the promise.
Genesis 32:28 supports Jacob's new name, but not the statement that he is Abraham's grandson. That relationship needs its own reference.
The passage does not say Abraham came for a talk or left afterward. It says God appeared to him and later went up from him.
The explanation is generic and closes with an instructional reminder rather than Papa Dorin's voice.
It places Abraham standing as he hears the promise, but he fell facedown before God spoke.
This is a flat, generic correction with little of Papa Dorin's voice.
The explanation simply repeats the answer and request without adding much explanation or Papa Dorin's personality.
The passage does not say whether Isaac is already conceived when God gives Abraham his name.
Genesis 37:3 names Joseph as Israel's son. A verse identifying Israel as Jacob is needed, along with a reference supporting Jacob's relationship to Abraham.
God says this time next year; the passage does not give Abraham a specific calendar date.
Saying where the timing got mixed up assumes why the baker chose the answer.
